summary.goal:
Extend this tiny todo library. Add to src/todo.js:
- toggle(id): flips the item's done flag and returns the item; throws an Error whose message contains "Unknown id" for an unknown id.
- remove(id): deletes the item and returns true, or returns false when the id is unknown.
- count(): returns the number of items.
Keep add(text) and list() working as they are (list returns a copy). Add tests for the new methods in test/ using node:test, and write a README.md that documents createStore, add, list, toggle, remove and count with a short example. npm test must stay green.

tasks.title: Implement toggle, remove and count in src/todo.js
tasks.spec:
Edit src/todo.js only. Extend the object returned by createStore() with the three new methods, keeping the existing terse single-line style.

Required semantics (see the frozen interface in the design doc):
- toggle(id): match the stored item whose id strictly equals id, flip its done boolean on the stored item, return that item object. If nothing matches, throw new Error('Unknown id: ' + id) — the message must contain the exact substring "Unknown id".
- remove(id): delete the matching item and return true; when no item matches return false and change nothing (no throw).
- count(): return the number of stored items.

Also change id assignment from `items.length + 1` to a private monotonic counter (e.g. `let nextId = 1` incremented on each add), so an add after a remove cannot reuse an id that is still in the store. Ids for add-only usage stay 1, 2, 3, … so this is not an observable change for existing callers.

Do not change add's or list's contract: add(text) still returns { id, text, done: false } appended in order, and list() still returns a new array (a copy) of the stored item objects in insertion order. Keep the file dependency-free ESM with the single named export createStore. Do not add tests here (separate task) and do not touch package.json or any other file.

acceptance.review: A green `npm test` only proves the pre-existing add/list test still passes. The reviewer must additionally confirm, by reading src/todo.js or by running a scratch script (e.g. `node --input-type=module -e "const {createStore}=await import('./src/todo.js'); const s=createStore(); s.add('a'); console.log(s.toggle(1), s.remove(1), s.count())"`): (1) toggle flips done and returns the same item object that list() exposes; (2) toggle on an unknown id throws an Error whose message contains 'Unknown id'; (3) remove returns true then, for the same id again, false without throwing; (4) count tracks adds and removes; (5) add after remove assigns an id that collides with no live item; (6) list() still returns a copy (mutating the result leaves the store unchanged).

report.summary: Added toggle, remove and count to the store returned by createStore in src/todo.js, and switched id assignment from `items.length + 1` to a private monotonic `nextId` counter so an add after a remove cannot reuse a live id. add's and list's contracts are unchanged (add still returns `{ id, text, done: false }` appended in order; list still returns a fresh array of the same item objects). The file stays dependency-free ESM with the single named export createStore, and only src/todo.js was touched.
report.evidence: `npm test` from the project root exits 0 (1 test, the pre-existing 'add and list', passes). A scratch `node --input-type=module` script confirmed every review point: count() is 0 on a fresh store; toggle(1) returns the identical object exposed by list() and flips done to true then back to false on a second call; toggle(99) throws an Error whose message contains 'Unknown id'; remove(1) returns true then false for the same id without throwing, with count dropping from 2 to 1; after removing id 1 an add gets id 3 (no collision with the live id 2, ids stay unique [2, 3]); and mutating the array returned by list() leaves the store unchanged (count still 2).
decisions: Used a `find`/`findIndex` with strict `===` id matching, and `items.splice` for removal so insertion order of the remaining items is preserved.
Kept the terse single-line method style of the existing file rather than splitting the methods across multiple lines.

tasks.title: Add node:test coverage for toggle, remove and count
tasks.spec:
Extend the existing test/todo.test.js (do not create a new file; `npm test` already globs test/*.test.js). Keep the existing 'add and list' test unchanged, and keep the file's conventions: `import test from 'node:test'`, `import assert from 'node:assert/strict'`, `import { createStore } from '../src/todo.js'`, one behavior per test, short descriptive names.

Add tests covering:
- add: ids are 1, 2, 3 in call order and each item starts with done === false and its text.
- list: returns a copy — push/splice on the returned array does not change what a second list() call returns, and count() is unaffected.
- count: 0 for a fresh store; increases per add; decreases after a remove.
- toggle: flips done false -> true and returns the item; a second toggle returns it to false; the returned object is the same object that appears in list() (assert identical reference or matching fields after a later list() call).
- toggle with an unknown id: throws, asserted with assert.throws using a /Unknown id/ matcher (message wording is part of the contract).
- remove: returns true, drops the item from list() and lowers count(); removing the same id a second time (or an id that never existed) returns false and leaves count() and list() unchanged.
- add after remove: the new item gets an id different from every id currently in list().

acceptance.review: Confirm the new tests genuinely exercise the new behavior: check out the pre-change src/todo.js (e.g. `git stash` the src change or read git show HEAD:src/todo.js) and verify the toggle/remove/count tests fail against it, then restore. Also confirm no test asserts on implementation details (no reaching into private state, no ordering assumptions beyond insertion order).

report.summary: Extended test/todo.test.js with 13 additional node:test tests covering add ids/shape, list copy semantics, count, toggle (flip, double flip, identity with list(), unknown-id throw), remove (true + removal, false for unknown and re-removed ids), and add-after-remove id uniqueness. The existing 'add and list' test and the import conventions were left unchanged, and no new file was created.
report.evidence: npm test from project root: exit 0, "tests 14 / pass 14 / fail 0". Review check against pre-change source: copied `git show HEAD:src/todo.js` and the new test file into a scratch dir, ran `node --test test/*.test.js` -> 12 of 14 fail (all new-behavior tests); only the pre-existing 'add and list' and the add-ids test pass, as expected since the old code already satisfies them. Scratch dir removed. `git status --porcelain` shows only src/todo.js (owned by the completed dependency task) and test/todo.test.js modified.
decisions: Extended the existing test/todo.test.js instead of creating a second file, since the test script already globs test/*.test.js.
Tests assert only through the public API (no private-state access); the sole ordering assumption is insertion order, used by the add-after-remove test to expect [b.id, c.id].
toggle error wording is pinned with assert.throws(..., /Unknown id/) as required by the frozen interface.

tasks.title: Write README.md documenting createStore, add, list, toggle, remove and count
tasks.spec:
Create README.md at the repository root (only this file). Plain Markdown, no badges, images, diagrams or external links.

Content:
1. Title `tiny-todo` and one sentence saying it is a tiny in-memory todo store with no dependencies.
2. A short 'Usage' section with a fenced ```js example, importable as written: import { createStore } from './src/todo.js', create a store, add two items, toggle the first, remove the second, then print the result of list() and count(). The example must be accurate against the implemented API — ids start at 1, add returns the item, toggle returns the toggled item, remove returns a boolean, count returns a number — and must not use unsupported syntax.
3. An 'API' section with one entry per member, each giving the signature, what it returns, and its error case: createStore(), add(text), list(), toggle(id), remove(id), count(). For toggle state that an unknown id throws an Error whose message contains 'Unknown id'; for remove that an unknown id returns false; for list that it returns a copy.
4. A 'Development' section stating that the tests use the built-in node:test runner and are run with `npm test`, and that Node 18 or newer is required. Do not add or change npm scripts.

Do not modify src/ or test/.

commands: for m in createStore add list toggle remove count; do grep -q "$m" README.md || exit 1; done
acceptance.review: Read the example code block and confirm it matches the implemented API exactly (ids starting at 1, return values, error text) and would run as ESM under Node without edits; confirm every one of the six members has its own documented entry and that the documented behavior matches src/todo.js.

It has a one-sentence intro, a Usage section with a runnable ESM example, an API section with an entry for each of createStore, add, list, toggle, remove and count, and a Development section noting node:test and `npm test` with Node 18+ required. decisions: The example uses the literal id 1 (from adding two items in order) for toggle and 2 for remove, since ids start at 1 and strictly increase; the printed list and count shown in comments were verified by actually executing the block.
Documented `npm test` as the existing script without adding or modifying any npm script, per the design's decision 6.
No badges, images, diagrams, external links or license section, per decision 5.
